launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.summary: A 985-acre Detroit River island park with beach, aquarium, conservatory, nature center, maritime museum, gardens, trails, paddling, playgrounds and skyline views.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.hours: Michigan DNR's statewide day-use rule lists 8:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m., while Belle Isle Conservancy currently posts 5:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. for the grounds. Because the official sources conflict, confirm posted entrance hours before an early visit; staffed attractions keep shorter schedules.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.parking: Parking is distributed across the island. A Michigan Recreation Passport is required for motor vehicles, while pedestrians, bicycles and public-transit riders enter without one. Route to the exact attraction before crossing the bridge.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.arrival: The MacArthur Bridge is the only road entrance. Choose the Aquarium/Conservatory complex, Nature Center, beach, Dossin museum, fountain or Kids Row before crossing because the island is nearly three miles long.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.restrooms: Restrooms and seasonal portable facilities are distributed around the island rather than available at every stop. Belle Isle Conservancy cautions that some bathrooms have limited accessibility, so confirm the nearest facility for a mobility-specific visit.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.cost: Park entry on foot, bicycle or transit is free. Motor vehicles require a Recreation Passport. Aquarium and conservatory admission are free; Dossin Museum, Giant Slide, rentals, golf and reservations have separate fees.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.accessibility: Accessible parking and developed routes exist at selected attractions, but the island is large and garden, green-space, picnic and some bathroom routes have documented limitations. Current construction can also change circulation.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed in ordinary outdoor areas under DNR rules but are restricted from park buildings, toilet buildings, designated swim beaches, endangered-species habitat and posted areas; service animals are exempt from building restrictions.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.family: Aquarium, conservatory, Nature Center, beach, Kids Row playground and Giant Slide can fill a day; verify each attraction's independent schedule and do not plan to cover the island from one parking space.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.transit: DDOT Route 12 Conant serves the island approximately hourly and stops at the Aquarium/Conservatory complex. Confirm the current weekday or Sunday schedule and the final walk to other attractions.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.need: The Scott Fountain plaza, adjacent sidewalk and Fountain Drive are closed through 2026, with reopening planned for spring 2027. The Aquarium remains open during renovation, and capacity controls can temporarily stop vehicle entry on busy summer afternoons.

launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.summary: A continuous public riverfront route of about 4.75 miles, linking Ralph Wilson Park west of downtown with plazas, play parks, state-park land, the east RiverWalk and Gabriel Richard Park near Belle Isle.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.hours: The RiverWalk, Conservancy parks and greenways are open daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Extended event hours and temporary closures may apply.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.parking: Select the intended segment on the Conservancy map before driving. Conservancy parks have associated free first-come lots, while greenway approaches, downtown meters, garages and neighboring attractions use different parking arrangements.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.arrival: Do not navigate to one generic RiverWalk pin. Pick Ralph Wilson Park, Cullen Plaza, Milliken State Park, Valade Park, Mt. Elliott, Gabriel Richard Park or another named segment and plan the return distance.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.restrooms: Restrooms are available at selected parks and facilities, not continuously along the path. Confirm the nearest open facility on the Conservancy map before starting a long one-way walk or ride.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.cost: Walking, cycling, parks and most play spaces are free. Parking outside Conservancy lots, carousel rides, food, rentals, events and neighboring attractions may cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.accessibility: The main promenade is paved with ramps and seating, but bridge approaches, distance, construction and temporary closures can interrupt a continuous route. Plan around a named segment rather than assuming the entire corridor is equivalent.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome under Conservancy rules. Keep pets under control, clean up waste and keep them out of play and water features.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.family: Valade's playground and beach, Mt. Elliott splash pad, Cullen carousel and Ralph Wilson Park create strong family stops, but each has separate seasonal operations and the full corridor is too long for many children.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.transit: People Mover, QLINE, DDOT buses, MoGo and downtown walking reach different segments; select transit around the intended park and return route rather than the corridor's midpoint.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.need: After 6:00 p.m., visitors under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian age 21 or older. Food, drink and water features are seasonal, swimming is prohibited, and major events can close individual segments.

launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.summary: Detroit's 22-acre west riverfront park with an expansive play garden, seasonal water play, an open-air sport house, courts, lawns, water garden, overlooks and direct RiverWalk connections.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.hours: The park is open daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. William Davidson Sport House closes at 8:00 p.m., Delta Dental Play Garden closes at 9:00 p.m., and seasonal Water Wonderland is listed 11:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. when operating.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.parking: About 150 free on-street spaces line West Jefferson and Rosa Parks. Paid parking and restrooms are available at Bagley Mobility Hub, 1501 Wabash Street, via Southwest Greenway; Assembly Garage is another paid option. Follow signs and expect event changes.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.arrival: The park spans West Jefferson between Eighth Street and Rosa Parks Boulevard. Walkers can arrive from downtown along the RiverWalk; Southwest Greenway connects from Bagley Mobility Hub, and each internal destination requires additional walking.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.restrooms: The park lists public restrooms, with additional facilities at Bagley Mobility Hub. Confirm same-day availability during events, maintenance or winter weather.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.cost: Park entry, play garden, water garden, Sport House courts, lawns and ordinary Conservancy programming are free. Parking, food and selected programs may cost separately; private rentals are not offered.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.accessibility: New paved routes connect major features, with inclusive play and seating distributed through the site. The Water Garden includes winding paths, a dock and bridge; visitors should use the exact route and avoid assuming every landscape surface is equivalent.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.dogs: Dogs and cats are allowed when leashed and under control. Keep pets out of active play, water-play and sport surfaces and away from the Water Garden shoreline.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.family: Delta Dental Play Garden, seasonal Water Wonderland and the open-air Sport House make this a strong free family destination, but each feature closes earlier than the surrounding park or operates seasonally.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.transit: DDOT routes 1, 27 and 29 serve the area. Southwest Greenway connects from Bagley Mobility Hub, and the Water Square People Mover station is about a half-mile east along the RiverWalk.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.need: This park opened in October 2025, so feature schedules and programming remain fast-changing. Verify Water Wonderland operation, Sport House hours, weather, parking and the event calendar before a feature-specific trip; fishing is prohibited in the Water Garden.

launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.address: Dequindre Cut at Atwater Street, Detroit, MI 48207
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.summary: A nearly two-mile below-grade paved greenway connecting the RiverWalk and Eastern Market, known for murals, separated walking and biking lanes, play elements, fitness equipment and a seasonal Freight Yard.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.hours: The Dequindre Cut is open daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. The Freight Yard, events and portable-restroom service keep shorter seasonal schedules.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.parking: The Cut has no designated parking lot. Use legal street parking near the chosen ramp; Freight Yard visitors may use the gravel lot at Wilkins and Orleans or nearby streets.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.arrival: Official ramps are at Atwater, Franklin, Woodbridge, Lafayette, Gratiot, Wilkins and Mack. Choose the ramp nearest the intended stop before entering the below-grade corridor.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.restrooms: There are no permanent restrooms. The operator places portable toilets near Campbell Terrace from April through October.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.cost: The greenway, murals, play elements and fitness equipment are free. Freight Yard food and drink and selected events cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.accessibility: The Cut has a 20-foot-wide paved path with separate pedestrian and bicycle lanes. Use an official ramp and account for its grade and the distance to the next exit.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.dogs: Leashed, controlled dogs are allowed under Conservancy rules. Keep pets on the pedestrian side and away from play areas and food service.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.family: Grand Trunks play elements and murals can make a memorable walk, but there are no permanent restrooms and exits are spaced apart.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.transit: The RiverWalk, Eastern Market, MoGo and nearby bus routes connect to different ramps; choose transit around the intended entrance and return distance.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.need: The Cut is below street level with limited quick exits. Note the nearest ramp, bring water in heat, and verify the Freight Yard and portable-restroom season before visiting.

launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.summary: Detroit's compact downtown gathering place with a summer beach, winter skating rink, lawn, dining, events and connections to adjacent public spaces.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.hours: The operator does not publish one dependable all-season park schedule. The Beach, Rink, Shop, dining areas and programmed events keep separate seasonal hours and may close for weather or setup.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.parking: Use paid downtown garages or legal metered parking and check current road closures. Event days and sports games can change access, prices and availability.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.arrival: Campus Martius sits at Woodward and Michigan avenues. Cadillac Square and Woodward Esplanade are adjacent but distinct public spaces, not destinations inside this park.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.restrooms: The operator does not identify a guaranteed stand-alone public restroom in the park. Plan around open businesses or staffed event facilities and verify access before relying on one.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.cost: Ordinary park seating, lawn and many events are free. Skating admission and rentals, food, drinks and parking cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.accessibility: The compact park uses paved routes and movable seating, but crowds, winter surfaces and event barricades can change circulation. Contact the operator for a specific accommodation.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.dogs: Do not assume pets may enter the seasonal beach, rink, dining or controlled-event areas. Follow current posted rules and keep any permitted dog leashed and controlled.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.family: The seasonal Beach, winter Rink and programmed events can work well for families, but each operates on its own schedule and rules.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.transit: QLINE, People Mover and DDOT routes converge nearby. Walking or transit is often easier than parking during downtown events.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.need: This small park changes substantially by season and event. Confirm the active setup before promising sand, skating, open lawn or ordinary through-access.

launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.summary: Detroit's 1,184-acre west-side regional park, with 4.6 miles of the Rouge River, more than 400 acres of forest, 60 acres of prairie, a five-acre marsh, paved paths, natural trails, recreation areas and golf.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.hours: Detroit park rules set ordinary park hours at 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Golf, organized camping, programs and construction-controlled facilities keep separate schedules; use remote natural trails in daylight.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.parking: Rouge Park has separate arrival areas rather than one central lot. The City's 2026 planning maps show parking near Brennan, golf, Joe Prance, trailheads and other active areas, but ongoing planning and construction can change access; choose the intended zone first.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.arrival: The official address is 21800 Joy Road, but this 1,184-acre park spans several roads. Use the City's current park map and route to Brennan, golf, Scout Hollow or a named trailhead instead of the parent pin.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.restrooms: The City does not promise a restroom at every recreation or natural area. Its 2026 planning materials identify existing and proposed comfort-station work, so verify the nearest open facility before entering a remote zone.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.cost: Ordinary park access, paved paths and natural areas are free. Golf, reservations, programs and authorized camping have separate arrangements and may cost extra.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.accessibility: The City documents six miles of paved walking paths, while natural hiking and mountain-bike trails cross forest, prairie and marsh terrain. The 2026 plan is still being developed, so confirm the exact paved route and current construction before a mobility-specific visit.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.dogs: Detroit park rules require dogs to stay on a leash no longer than 72 inches, require waste cleanup and prohibit pets in play areas, on play equipment and on sports fields. Follow additional posted restrictions near facilities and habitat work.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.family: Developed recreation areas and paved paths provide family options, but Brennan Pool is closed for construction and the park's scale and remote natural areas require a chosen destination and return plan.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.transit: DDOT Route 27 Joy serves the Joy Road corridor on a schedule that changed in April 2026. Check the current stop and timetable, then account for the long distance from the park edge to the selected internal destination.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.need: Brennan Pool is closed for construction until 2027 while a new recreation facility is built. The Rouge Park master plan remains in development, and lighting, camera, prairie-restoration and facility work can change individual approaches.

launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.summary: A 281-acre north Detroit regional park with Lake Frances, a historic log cabin, Witherell Woods, a new bandshell, dog park, splash park, playground, courts, fields and fitness areas.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.hours: Detroit park rules set ordinary hours at 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m.; the City's Adopt-a-Park partner says winter access is limited to daylight hours. Splash play, Log Cabin interiors and bandshell programs keep seasonal or event schedules.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.parking: Use Merrill Plaisance and Woodward Avenue for the Lake Frances and Log Cabin area. The City documents a new 60-space paved lot at the bandshell; large events can fill or control nearby parking.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.arrival: Use Merrill Plaisance for Lake Frances, the Log Cabin and the historic core. The dog park and bandshell are approached from the Seven Mile Road side, while recreation facilities farther south require their own arrival point.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.restrooms: The City documents new restrooms at the bandshell complex but does not promise that they remain unlocked outside programmed events. Verify access before relying on them elsewhere in the 281-acre park.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.cost: Ordinary park access is free. The dog park and seasonal splash park are free; reservations, special events and programs may have separate registration or costs.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.accessibility: The City documents newer paved walkways, parking, playground and gathering areas, but does not certify every route. Witherell Woods remains natural terrain, and the exact condition of older facilities should be confirmed for a mobility-specific visit.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.dogs: Detroit park rules require a leash no longer than 72 inches outside the fenced dog park and prohibit pets in play areas and sports fields. The one-acre dog park has separate small- and large-dog areas, drinking fountains and waste stations.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.family: The playground, summer splash park, Lake Frances, courts and 2026 community programs offer varied family stops. Keep children close at the lake and verify the independent schedule for water play or Cabin access.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.transit: DDOT Route 4 Woodward serves the east edge of Palmer Park, and the City identifies a mobility hub at Woodward and Merrill Plaisance. Confirm the current stop and the walk to the selected feature.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.need: The splash park is seasonal, the Log Cabin interior opens for announced programs rather than daily tours, and bandshell events can control parking and restroom access. The City still presents Lake Frances and Witherell Woods habitat work as an active park project.

launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.summary: Detroit's riverfront civic plaza and festival ground, centered on the restored Dodge Fountain and surrounded by major public art, terraces and event spaces.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.hours: The City lists Hart Plaza as open year-round but does not publish one dependable daily-hours window. Festivals, setup, security screening and maintenance can replace ordinary access.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.parking: Use paid downtown garages or legal meters and check the event traffic plan. Festivals, fireworks, Grand Prix and sports days can cause closures, controlled access and special prices.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.arrival: Approach from Jefferson Avenue, the RiverWalk or downtown transit. During events, use the official gate and current prohibited-item instructions rather than an everyday plaza entrance.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.restrooms: The City does not promise an always-open public restroom outside staffed events. Festivals may add controlled facilities inside their perimeter; verify before relying on one.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.cost: Ordinary plaza and public-art viewing are free. Events may be free or ticketed, and parking costs separately.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.accessibility: Broad paved terraces connect downtown and the river, but ramps, stairs, fountain conditions and event barricades affect routes. Contact the City or event organizer for a specific accommodation.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.dogs: Do not assume pets are admitted during events. Security-controlled programs can prohibit them; follow the current event rules and posted ordinary-use restrictions.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.family: Public art and river views make an easy short stop, while crowded festivals require hearing protection, identification plans and event-specific preparation for children.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.transit: Financial District is the closest People Mover station identified by the City for a 2026 Hart Plaza event. QLINE and DDOT also serve downtown, and the RiverWalk connects on foot.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.need: Hart Plaza is an event venue as much as a public square. Check the City's 2026 event calendar, closures, ticket rules and security restrictions before every visit.
